Surp Hagop Church (Armenian: Սուրբ Յակոբ Եկեղեցի); also Saint Jacob or Saint James, is a small Armenian Apostolic church, located on al-Iman street in Old Syriac (Assyrian) quarter of Aleppo, Syria. Opened 1943, enlarged 1962.

Ground blessing ceremony took place 3 June 1934, during period Archbishop Ardavazt Surmeyan, on land around 750 square meters, donated by Italian General Consul Georgio Marcopolli. Construction started 1940, with erection of small building. Consecration took place 1943 with presence of community leaders. Church was named honour of Saint Jacob of Nisibis.

Current shape dates back to 1962, after major enlargement. Surrounded with small yard, church is without dome and belfry.

In 1988–89, church completely renovated by Armenian Diocese of Beroea.

Biblical narrative

According to Genesis (Chapter 28:10-22), Jacob was fleeing from elder twin brother Esau, whom he had cheated out of father's blessing. On flight, Jacob rested at Luz and used stones as pillow.

11 And he took of stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down to sleep.

15 I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and bring thee again into this land; I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken.

Energy subsidies are government payments that keep price of energy lower than market rate for consumers or higher than market rate for producers. These subsidies are part of energy policy of United States.

According to Congressional Budget Office testimony in 2016, $10.9 billion in tax preferences was directed toward renewable energy, $4.6 billion went to fossil fuels, and $2.7 billion went to energy efficiency or electricity transmission.

According to 2015 estimate by Obama administration, US oil industry benefited from subsidies about $4.6 billion per year. A 2017 study by researchers at Stockholm Environment Institute estimated that "tax preferences and other subsidies push nearly half of new, yet-to-be-developed oil investments into profitability."

Biofuel subsidies

In United States, biofuel subsidies have been justified on grounds: energy independence, reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, rural development and farm income support. Several economists found "there is no evidence to disprove that primary objective of biofuel policy is to support farm income."

Consumer subsidies

Consumers who purchase hybrid vehicles are eligible for tax credit depending upon type of vehicle and difference in fuel economy. Homeowners can receive tax credit up to $500 for energy-efficient products. Homeowners who install solar electric systems can receive 30% tax credit and small wind systems tax credit up to $4000. Geothermal heat pumps qualify for tax credits up to $2,000.

Other subsidies

Recent energy policy incentives have provided billions of dollars in tax reductions for nuclear power, fossil fuel production, clean coal technologies, renewable electricity production, and conservation and efficiency improvements.
